threads.thread_goal: Align on current routines, constraints, and select pilot group for the program.

messages.text:
Starting this thread to kick off the Integrated Wellbeing Program for At-Risk Youth Group Home project_title. Aim here is to get a shared picture of current routines and agree who joins the first pilot group.

We need to complete the mapping in task T1 and keep the overview in artifact A1 up to date. That will help us see realistic time windows for structured activities on weekdays.

First questions:
- Which 6–8 youths do you feel are suitable for the first pilot group (thinking about motivation, stability, and consent)?
- Can we list the fixed points in the week: school hours, therapy, contact visits, and any regular external activities?

@36599 and @4543, could you start by listing current weekday patterns for the youths you know best, including usual wake-up, school, after-school, and evening routines? @87396, it would help if you flag any existing vocational or work-related commitments you are aware of.

Once we have that, we can confirm the time windows for the pilot and then agree on the initial group.

Thanks for starting this. I can start filling in task T1 for the younger group and add it into artifact A1 once I have it in a simple table.

Quick overview from what I see on late shifts:
- Weekdays: most are out at school roughly 8:30–14:30, two of the older ones sometimes stay until 15:30.
- After school: snack and decompress usually 15:00–16:00, then a mix of gaming, hanging out in rooms, or going outside.
- Evenings: dinner around 18:00, then chores and free time. Bedtime routines start around 21:00, but it varies.

For possible pilot youths, my first thoughts (using initials only here):
- J: usually joins group activities and has asked for more structure.
- L: calmer lately, likes cooking and crafts.
- M: can be restless but responds well when given a clear role.

I will check with the rest of the team on shift tonight to see who else they suggest and who might find extra structure overwhelming right now.

I can help with the mapping too, but I might need a bit of guidance on how detailed we want artifact A1 to be.

From my morning shifts:
- Most of the group wakes up between 6:45 and 7:15.
- Breakfast and meds (for those who have them) are usually done by 7:45.
- Transport to school is 8:00–8:20.

We also have:
- One youth with weekly therapy on Tuesday at 16:00.
- Another with contact visit every second Thursday from 17:00.

For the pilot group, I agree with J and L. I am less sure about M because of some recent conflicts in the evenings, but maybe that is exactly where structure could help. I would like to hear your view on that before we confirm.

From the vocational side, I can add a few constraints and also some ideas for who might benefit most.

Constraints I see:
- Two of the older youths have occasional trial shifts at a local workshop on Thursdays 14:00–16:00.
- One youth attends an external skills group on Mondays 16:00–18:00.

I will add these into artifact A1 so they are visible for task T1.

For the pilot group, I would suggest including at least three youths who have already shown interest in practical tasks (cooking, fixing things, helping staff). J and L fit that. I would also consider N, who often asks about jobs but then withdraws when things feel too formal. A gentle, in-house pilot could be a good bridge for N.

We should also check with the youths themselves and get their agreement before we finalise the list.

This is helpful, thank you. For artifact A1, let us keep it simple: blocks of time rather than minute-by-minute. For example: school, free time, meals, therapy, visits.

On M: I share the concern about recent conflicts. At the same time, the project objective is to align care, pedagogy, and skills, so it would be good not to exclude youths who struggle more, as long as we can keep it safe.

How about this as a working idea:
- Core pilot group: J, L, N.
- Optional participants: M and one more, depending on their own interest and current stability.

Before we confirm, could you both check in your next shifts how J, L, N, and M feel about joining a new weekly program that mixes fun, learning, and practical skills? We should be clear that participation is voluntary and not a reward or punishment.

I can talk with J, L, and M tonight in a relaxed way and see how they react. I will also ask if they have any worries about joining a more structured weekly thing.

For N, I am on shift tomorrow afternoon and can check in then. I will note their responses in a short list and share here so we can decide together.

On time windows, based on what we have so far, I see two possible weekday slots:
- After school, roughly 16:00–17:30.
- Early evening, roughly 19:00–20:00 on days without visits or therapy.

We need to be careful not to clash with existing routines that help them calm down before bed.

I will also talk with them in the morning when things are usually calmer. I can ask simple questions like what kind of group activities they enjoy and if they would like to try something new once or twice a week.

About time windows, I am a bit unsure if 19:00–20:00 is too late for some of the younger ones, especially on school nights. Maybe we could keep that slot lighter, like short check-ins or games, and use the 16:00–17:30 slot for more structured parts.

I will add the morning routine blocks into artifact A1 later today so we have the full picture for task T1.

Agree that 16:00–17:30 looks like the main window for more structured activities, especially anything that needs focus, like short vocational tasters later on.

From what I have seen, Wednesdays and Fridays tend to be a bit lighter in terms of external appointments. Could we tentatively mark:
- One main structured block on Wednesday 16:00–17:30.
- One lighter or optional block on Friday 16:00–17:00.

We can still adjust once task T1 is fully mapped in artifact A1, but it would help me start thinking about where vocational elements might fit without clashing with school or therapy.

Provisional slots sound reasonable. Let us treat them as draft until we have the full week mapped.

To move forward, we need two things in this thread:
1) Confirm the pilot group.
2) Confirm the time windows for structured activities on weekdays.

Once @36599 and @4543 have spoken with J, L, N, and M, could you post a short summary of who is interested and any clear no from the youths? Then we can finalise the group and the time windows in one go.

Quick update after last night and this afternoon:
- J: clearly interested, asked if there will be cooking and music.
- L: positive, said they like having something planned so they know what is coming.
- M: mixed. Said they want to join if it is not too strict and if they can sometimes step out when they feel overwhelmed.
- N: hesitant but curious. Asked if it is ok to just watch at first.

No one said a clear no. I explained that it is voluntary and that they can give feedback after a few weeks.

Based on this, I would be comfortable including all four, as long as we build in options to step back when needed.

From my morning talks:
- J and L both asked when it would start.
- M said they do not want anything that feels like school, but they were ok when I said there will also be games and practical things.
- N asked if they can choose some of the activities.

I agree that we can include all four, but we should be careful with expectations and keep checking in with them.

On time windows, I still feel that 16:00–17:30 works best for the main part. Maybe we can keep 19:00–20:00 as an optional, lighter slot once a week, not every day.

Including all four makes sense to me, especially if we are clear that they can step out or just observe at times. That fits with the idea of keeping participation voluntary and non-stigmatising.

On timing, I support:
- Main structured block: Wednesday 16:00–17:30.
- Second block: Friday 16:00–17:00, lighter and more flexible.
- Optional short check-in or game slot: one evening 19:00–19:30, maybe Tuesday, if staff capacity allows.

If we agree on this, I can already start sketching where vocational tasters might sit later, without locking anything yet.

Thanks for gathering the youths views. To close this thread, I suggest we make two clear agreements now.

Proposal for the pilot group:
- J, L, M, and N as the initial pilot youths.

Proposal for weekday time windows:
- Main structured sessions on Wednesdays 16:00–17:30.
- Additional structured or lighter sessions on Fridays 16:00–17:00.
- Optional short check-in or game slot once a week around 19:00–19:30, only if staffing on that day is sufficient.

Unless there are strong objections by tomorrow morning, I will treat this as agreed so we can move on to designing the weekly schedule.

Works for me. The times fit with what we see on shifts, and the four youths have all shown at least some interest.

I will keep updating artifact A1 for task T1 as we notice any changes in routines, especially new appointments or visits that might affect these slots.

No objections from me. The agreed group and time windows give us a clear frame for the next steps.

I will keep Thursdays free from any pilot activities on my side, given the workshop trial shifts, and focus my planning around the Wednesday and Friday blocks.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the weekly structured activity schedule and co-designed activities.

messages.text:
Starting this thread to share the first draft of the weekly structured activity schedule for the pilot group and get your comments.

Based on artifact A1 and our earlier decision on time windows, I have drafted a simple version of artifact A5 and linked it to task T3. The idea is to balance education support, leisure, social skills, and space for vocational tasters.

Current draft for the four pilot youths (J, L, M, N):
- Wednesday 16:00–16:20: arrival, snack, and check-in.
- 16:20–17:00: group activity focused on social skills or cooperation.
- 17:00–17:30: lighter activity or preparation for vocational tasters.

- Friday 16:00–16:20: short check-in and feedback on the week.
- 16:20–17:00: co-designed activity (to be defined with the youths).

I have left one evening 19:00–19:30 slot open as optional, not every week, for games or calm activities.

I need your help to:
1) Refine the structure so it is realistic for shifts.
2) Decide which co-designed activities from task T6 we include.

Please share what you see working or not working in practice.

Thanks for putting this together. From a shift point of view, the Wednesday structure looks manageable.

On co-designed activities for task T6, I have already started a small list from informal chats:
- J and L both suggested a cooking club where they can help plan and cook a simple meal.
- M and N mentioned a music and games evening, with some time for playlists and maybe simple board games.

I think we could shape these into two clear activities with goals and simple rules. For example:
- Cooking club: once every two weeks on Wednesday or Friday.
- Music and games: lighter Friday slot or the optional evening slot.

We need to check how this fits with staff capacity in the kitchen and common areas.

I like the idea of starting with a check-in and snack. That usually helps them settle.

One concern: on some Wednesdays, homework can take longer, especially if there are tests. Maybe we should build in a bit more flexibility at the start, so they can join even if they are 10–15 minutes late.

For co-designed activities, I have heard:
- J wants to try a simple baking session.
- L asked about arts and crafts.

Could we combine these into a rotating creative block on Fridays, where one week is cooking or baking, another week is crafts? That might keep it fresh without overloading staff.

From my side, the Wednesday 16:20–17:00 block is a good place to occasionally introduce very light vocational tasters later, as long as we keep them practical and short.

For now, I suggest we treat the first three weeks as mainly about group cohesion and co-designed activities. Once that feels stable, we can start weaving in small vocational elements that connect to what they already enjoy, like cooking or simple repair tasks.

On the schedule in artifact A5, I would recommend we:
- Mark clearly which weeks have cooking club versus crafts.
- Keep the optional evening slot strictly low-pressure, maybe linked to music and games as suggested.

This will also make it easier to align with task T5 later.

Good points about homework and flexibility. We can adjust the Wednesday start like this:
- 16:00–16:30: open arrival, snack, and informal check-in, with space for homework finishing.
- 16:30–17:10: main group activity.
- 17:10–17:30: cool-down and transition.

On co-designed activities for task T6, I hear at least two clear ideas:
1) Cooking and baking club.
2) Music and games / creative block (including crafts).

If we document these with simple goals and rules, they can become our two main co-designed activities.

Does this structure feel workable on your shifts?

Yes, the adjusted Wednesday timing feels more realistic. It gives us room to handle late arrivals without making anyone feel they have failed.

For the two co-designed activities, I can start drafting short descriptions for task T6:
- Cooking and baking club: goal is to practice basic kitchen skills and cooperation, with clear safety rules.
- Music, games, and crafts: goal is to relax together, share interests, and practice turn-taking and respect.

I will test these ideas with the youths this week and see if they want to add or change anything before we lock them into artifact A5.

The structure looks ok to me. I just want to flag that on some Fridays, staff numbers are a bit tighter around dinner prep. If we do cooking club on Fridays, we need to plan simple recipes and make sure there is enough supervision.

Maybe we could:
- Use Wednesday for cooking or baking when possible, since there is a bit more time.
- Keep Friday more for music, games, and crafts, which are easier to scale up or down depending on how many staff are free.

I can help write down the basic rules for the activities once we agree on which day they sit on.

That makes sense. From a practical point of view, cooking on Wednesdays also gives us more time to clean up without rushing into dinner.

How about this arrangement in artifact A5:
- Wednesday: main structured block, alternating between social skills games and cooking/baking.
- Friday: lighter block focused on music, games, and crafts, with space for the youths to bring their own ideas.

This still gives us two clear co-designed activities for task T6 and keeps the workload manageable.

I like this arrangement. To summarise the current draft schedule in artifact A5 for task T3:

Wednesday
- 16:00–16:30: open arrival, snack, and informal check-in.
- 16:30–17:10: main activity (alternating weekly between social skills games and cooking/baking).
- 17:10–17:30: cool-down and transition.

Friday
- 16:00–16:20: short check-in and week reflection.
- 16:20–17:00: music, games, and crafts block, shaped with the youths.

Optional
- One evening 19:00–19:30 every second week for a calm game or music session, only if staffing allows.

If you both are ok with this, we can treat cooking/baking and music/games/crafts as the two main co-designed activities for the pilot.

This summary matches what we have discussed and feels workable on the floor.

I will present the two co-designed activities to the youths as:
- Cooking and baking club on some Wednesdays.
- Music, games, and crafts on Fridays.

I will also check if they have any small adjustments before we start the first week, but I do not expect big changes.

No objections from me. The schedule is clear and leaves enough room to gradually introduce vocational tasters that connect to cooking and practical tasks.

From my side, this is a good initial weekly structured activity schedule for the pilot. Once we see it in action for a couple of weeks, we can fine-tune details, but I would be comfortable calling this our starting point.

Great, then let us formally treat this as the approved initial weekly structured activity schedule for the pilot, with the two co-designed activities we have defined.

I will update artifact A5 accordingly and mark task T3 as drafted. We can still adjust after the first weeks, but this gives us a clear framework to brief the rest of the team.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on templates and tools: individual plans, handover checklist, and monitoring log.

messages.text:
Opening this thread to review the draft templates and tools before we start the pilot.

I have uploaded:
- Draft Individual Support and Development Plan template as artifact A2, linked to task T2.
- Draft Shift Handover and Coordination Checklist as artifact A4, linked to task T7.
- Draft Wellbeing and Engagement Monitoring Log as artifact A7, linked to task T8.

The aim is to keep all three simple enough for all shifts to use, while still covering wellbeing, social development, and any risks.

Could you please look at:
- Are there any sections in A2 that feel unclear or too long?
- Does A4 cover the key points you need at handover?
- Are the indicators and rating scale in A7 realistic to fill in without adding too much workload?

I would like us to agree on final versions here so we can start using them from the first pilot week.

I have gone through the drafts.

On artifact A2 (individual plan):
- I like that it is one page per youth.
- The wellbeing and social skills sections are clear.
- The risk indicators part might need simpler wording so that night staff and new colleagues understand it the same way.

On artifact A4 (handover checklist):
- The mood, incidents, and appointments boxes are very helpful.
- Could we add a small line for 'youth requests or ideas' so we do not lose what they tell us informally?

On artifact A7 (monitoring log):
- The 0–3 scale for participation and mood seems ok.
- I worry that filling it every day for each youth might be too much. Maybe we could focus on the four pilot youths and do it three times a week instead of daily.

I also had a look, but I am not fully sure if I understood all parts correctly.

For artifact A2, the section about education and future plans feels a bit open. Maybe we could add examples, like 'support with homework' or 'interest in cooking' so staff know what to write.

For artifact A4, I like that it reminds us to note mood and any incidents. Sometimes we forget small things that later turn out to be important.

For artifact A7, I agree with @36599 that doing it every day for everyone might be hard. I would find it easier if we had clear instructions on when exactly to fill it in, for example at the end of the Wednesday and Friday sessions.

From my perspective:

Artifact A2:
- The template covers wellbeing, social skills, education, and future orientation, which is good.
- I would suggest adding one short line under education/future for 'practical skills interests' so we can note things like cooking, fixing bikes, or digital skills.

Artifact A4:
- The checklist looks solid. I support adding a line for 'youth requests or ideas' as @36599 suggested.

Artifact A7:
- For the pilot, I would focus the monitoring on the four pilot youths only.
- A simple 0–3 scale for participation, mood, and conflicts, filled in after each structured session (Wednesday and Friday), should give us enough data without overloading staff.

This would keep tasks T2, T7, and T8 aligned with the project constraint about not over-assessing.

Thank you all, this is very helpful.

Based on your feedback, I propose the following adjustments:

Artifact A2 (individual plan):
- Simplify wording in the risk indicators section.
- Add examples under education and future plans.
- Add a line for 'practical skills interests'.

Artifact A4 (handover checklist):
- Add a line for 'youth requests or ideas'.

Artifact A7 (monitoring log):
- Focus only on the four pilot youths.
- Use a 0–3 scale for participation, mood, and conflicts.
- Fill it in after each structured session (Wednesday and Friday), not daily.

If you agree, I will update A2, A4, and A7 accordingly and then we can confirm them as our tools for the pilot.

These adjustments address my concerns.

With the simpler wording and examples, I think artifact A2 will be easier for all shifts to use.

The added line in artifact A4 for youth requests or ideas will help us keep track of what they tell us in passing.

And limiting artifact A7 to the four pilot youths and to the structured sessions feels realistic. I can help explain this to colleagues during handovers so everyone knows when to fill it in.

I agree with these changes as well.

Having examples in artifact A2 will make it less intimidating to fill in.

The updated artifact A4 will remind me to pass on small but important things the youths say.

For artifact A7, filling it in after the Wednesday and Friday sessions is clear. I might still need a reminder at first, but once it becomes routine it should be fine.

No further changes from my side. The tools now look aligned with what we need for the pilot.

Once you have updated artifacts A2, A4, and A7, I suggest we treat them as our agreed templates and start using them from the first structured session.

Great, I will make the edits now and re-upload the updated versions of artifacts A2, A4, and A7.

Once that is done, I would like us to formally agree that:
- The Individual Support and Development Plan template in A2 is approved for use with the four pilot youths.
- The shift handover checklist in A4 and the monitoring indicators and scale in A7 are our final versions for the pilot.

Unless there are new concerns by tomorrow, I will consider these tools approved and move tasks T2, T7, and T8 to done for the pilot phase.
Fine with me. I will start using artifact A2 for J, L, M, and N as soon as the updated version is up, and I will encourage colleagues to use artifacts A4 and A7 as agreed.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate vocational skills taster modules within the weekly schedule.

messages.text:
Starting this thread to propose vocational skills taster modules and check how they can fit into our weekly schedule.

I have drafted three short modules for artifact A6, linked to task T5:
1) Basic cooking skills: simple recipes, kitchen safety, and working together.
2) Everyday practical skills: small repairs, basic tool use, and looking after shared spaces.
3) Future steps and CV basics: talking about strengths, simple CV elements, and practice with short introductions.

Each module is designed as 2–3 short sessions of 30–40 minutes, with clear objectives and minimal materials.

Questions for you:
- Which of these modules should we run in the first pilot cycle with J, L, M, and N?
- Looking at artifact A5, which exact days and times work best so we do not clash with school, therapy, or the main group activities?

Once we agree, I can finalise artifact A6 and plan the first sessions for task T9.

These modules sound very relevant for our group.

For the first pilot cycle, I would prioritise:
- Basic cooking skills, since J and L are already interested and it links to our cooking club.
- Everyday practical skills, as M and N often ask about doing more hands-on things.

The future steps and CV basics module might be better once they are more comfortable with the program, maybe in a second cycle.

Looking at artifact A5, I see two options:
- Use part of the Wednesday 16:30–17:10 block every second week for a short vocational focus.
- Or add a separate 30-minute slot once a week, maybe Thursday 16:00–16:30, if that does not clash with the workshop trial shifts you mentioned earlier.

I agree that cooking and practical skills fit well with what the youths have been asking for.

I am a bit worried about adding too much on Wednesdays, because that is already our main structured day. Maybe we could:
- Keep Wednesdays mainly for the group activities we already planned.
- Use a shorter slot on Fridays or another weekday for the vocational tasters, so it feels like something extra but not overwhelming.

We also need to be careful with Thursdays because of the workshop trial shifts for two of the older youths, even if they are not in the pilot group yet.

From a coordination point of view, I would also start with the two more practical modules: basic cooking skills and everyday practical skills.

On timing, we need to respect the constraints we mapped in artifact A1 and the structure in artifact A5. I see two realistic options:
1) Integrate short tasters into the Wednesday main block every second week, replacing part of the usual activity.
2) Create a separate, small slot on a day with fewer external commitments, for example Monday 16:00–16:30, if that does not clash with the external skills group you mentioned.

We should avoid Thursdays because of the workshop trial shifts. Could you confirm, @87396, whether Monday 16:00–16:30 is free enough for the four pilot youths?

Good points.

On content: I agree we start with
- Module 1: Basic cooking skills.
- Module 2: Everyday practical skills.

We can keep Module 3 (future steps and CV basics) for a later cycle once trust is stronger.

On timing: one of the youths has an external skills group on Monday 16:00–18:00, so Monday 16:00–16:30 would not work for the whole pilot group.

Looking again at artifact A5 and the constraints in artifact A1, I suggest:
- Use the Friday 16:20–17:00 block once every two weeks for a vocational taster, alternating between cooking skills and practical skills.
- On the alternate Fridays, keep it as the usual music, games, and crafts block.

This way we do not add extra sessions, we just shape some of the existing time with a clearer vocational focus.

Alternating Fridays sounds like a good compromise. It keeps the rhythm simple for staff and youths:
- One Friday more vocational and hands-on.
- One Friday more relaxed with music and games.

For the first pilot cycle, I would suggest we plan:
- Two sessions of basic cooking skills.
- Two sessions of everyday practical skills.

That should be enough to see how the group responds without overloading them.

I can work with alternating Fridays. It will be important to make it clear on the schedule which Friday is which, so we can prepare materials and the youths know what to expect.

For the cooking module, please keep recipes simple and low-risk, like sandwiches, salads, or baking something small. That will make it easier for us to manage safety and clean-up within the time.

Noted on keeping recipes simple and safe.

To summarise the proposal for the first pilot cycle:
- Modules to run: Basic cooking skills and Everyday practical skills.
- Each module: two sessions of about 35–40 minutes.
- Timing: Friday 16:20–17:00 every week, alternating between vocational sessions and the usual music/games/crafts.

If we agree on this, I will finalise artifact A6 with detailed objectives, duration, and materials for these two modules and align it with artifact A5. Then we can schedule the first vocational session for the second Friday of the pilot, giving us one week to settle into the routine first.

This summary works for me and fits with the constraints we mapped earlier.

So for clarity:
- Confirmed modules for the first pilot cycle: Basic cooking skills and Everyday practical skills.
- Confirmed timing: Friday 16:20–17:00, alternating with the regular music/games/crafts block, avoiding clashes with school, therapy, and workshop shifts.

I will update artifact A5 to reflect which Fridays are vocational and which are not, so staff can see it at a glance.
Agreed from my side as well. I will start telling J, L, M, and N that some Fridays will have a more practical focus, and I will collect their quick feedback after the first sessions for task T9.

threads.thread_goal: Review first two weeks of pilot, discuss incidents, and agree on adjustments.

messages.text:
We are two weeks into the pilot, so I am sharing a short summary and asking for your views on what to adjust.

I have compiled feedback from youths and staff into artifact A8, linked to task T11, and looked at the first entries in artifact A7.

Key points:
- Participation: J and L have attended almost all sessions; M and N have joined most but sometimes stepped out early.
- Mood: overall calmer during structured times, but M had one incident last Wednesday when a game became too competitive.
- Co-designed activities: cooking/baking and music/games/crafts are clearly the favourites, but sessions feel a bit rushed on some days.
- Vocational tasters: we have not yet run a full vocational session, but we did a short trial of basic knife skills during cooking.

There was one moment last week where M showed early signs of distress. Staff followed the steps in artifact A3 (crisis and trauma-support guide), moved M to a quieter space, and debriefed afterwards.

I would like us to:
- Revisit the composition of the pilot group if needed.
- Decide which co-designed activities to keep as they are, which to modify, and whether we need a new one.

Please share your observations from shifts and any suggestions for adjustments for task T12.

From what I have seen on late shifts:

Pilot group:
- J and L are clearly benefiting. They talk about the sessions afterwards and seem proud of what they cooked or created.
- M has had ups and downs. The incident you mentioned started when they felt teased during a game. Using the steps from artifact A3 helped, but it showed we need clearer rules around games.
- N often starts by watching and then joins in halfway. They told me they like that they can choose how much to join.

Co-designed activities:
- Cooking/baking works very well, but we need a bit more time for clean-up.
- Music/games/crafts is popular, but some games trigger competition and frustration.

My suggestions:
- Keep all four youths in the pilot group for now, but keep checking in with M about how they feel.
- Keep cooking/baking as is, but extend the cool-down time.
- Adjust the music/games/crafts block to include more cooperative games and fewer competitive ones.

I agree with most of what @36599 wrote.

On the incident with M, I was on shift and noticed early signs like restlessness and louder voice. We followed artifact A3 by:
- Offering a short break.
- Moving to a quieter corner.
- Checking in about what was upsetting them.

It calmed down, but it reminded me that we need to be careful with activities that can feel like winning and losing.

For adjustments:
- I would keep the same four youths in the pilot group. M told me later they still want to join, just with fewer competitive games.
- Maybe we could add a new calm activity option, like drawing or simple crafts, that they can switch to when they feel overwhelmed.

From the small vocational elements we tried:
- The basic knife skills during cooking went well when we kept it one youth at a time with close supervision.
- J and L were very engaged; M and N preferred to watch first.

Looking at artifact A7, participation scores are highest on cooking days and slightly lower on some of the games sessions.

I would support:
- Keeping the pilot group as is, with extra attention to M.
- Keeping cooking/baking as a core activity.
- Adjusting the music/games/crafts block to focus more on cooperative or creative tasks.

For task T12, we could also consider adding a very simple new co-designed activity, like a 'chill corner' with drawing and music for those who need a quieter option.

Thank you for these detailed observations.

On the pilot group composition:
- It sounds like all four youths are still engaged and want to continue, even if M needs some adjustments.

On co-designed activities:
- Cooking/baking is clearly a keeper.
- Music/games/crafts needs some reshaping to reduce competitive elements.
- A calm 'chill corner' option could be a useful addition, especially for M and N.

I propose we:
1) Keep J, L, M, and N in the pilot group, with a note in their individual plans about how they prefer to participate.
2) Keep cooking/baking as a main activity.
3) Modify the music/games/crafts block to focus on cooperative games and creative tasks.
4) Add a simple calm corner option as part of that block.

Please say if you disagree with any of these points before we record them as our agreed adjustments.

I agree with all four points.

For the calm corner, we can set up a small table with drawing materials and headphones with calm music. We can explain to the youths that it is ok to move there when they need a break, without making it feel like they are being sent away.

I can also update the notes in artifact A2 for each youth to reflect their preferred ways of taking breaks and what helps them calm down.

Works for me too.

I will be careful to choose games that are more about working together than winning, like building something as a group or cooperative board games.
